alerts.title: Untreated hypothyroidism mimics DTG weight gain
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycemia risk factors before DTG use, with BMI ≥25 as a risk factor. This patient has BMI 33 and age 45, meeting 2 risk factors requiring glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year. However, her TSH is 12.4 mIU/L with low Free T4, indicating inadequately treated hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting levothyroxine. Symptoms of weight gain (9 kg), tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes are classic hypothyroidism signs. Evidence against DTG attribution: symptom profile and biochemical hypothyroidism strongly suggest the weight gain and metabolic changes are primarily thyroid-driven rather than DTG-related. Switching DTG may not resolve symptoms if hypothyroidism remains untreated.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimize levothyroxine adherence and dose before attributing weight gain to DTG. Recheck TSH after 6-8 weeks of consistent dosing. Address adherence barriers before considering DTG switch.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycemia risk with BMI ≥25 and age ≥40
alerts.message: Guidelines state adults on DTG with 2 or more hyperglycemia risk factors (age ≥40, BMI ≥24, hypertension history) need glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year. This patient has age 45 and BMI 33, meeting 2 risk factors. Fasting glucose today is 5.6 mmol/L, below the high threshold of >6.95. No glucose checks are documented in the clinician's plan. While her current glucose is acceptable, monitoring gaps exist given her risk profile and the metabolic derangements seen today.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform fasting or random blood glucose every 3 months. Given deranged lipids and BMI 33, reinforce lifestyle counselling and consider dietary intervention.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by 6 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The patient's last creatinine was 196 days before this visit (approximately 6 months ago), making the next annual check due in approximately 6 months. However, no renal monitoring is included in today's plan. While the 12-month interval has not fully elapsed, confirming renal function alongside today's metabolic panel would be good practice.

evidence.recommended_action: Document schedule for annual creatinine and eGFR. Consider checking today since the patient is already having blood drawn for other labs.

Hyperglycemia among previously non-diabetic adults and worsening of hyperglycemia among diabetics has been reported among clients on DTG. Although the hyperglycemia associated with DTG has been reported among clients newly initiated on ART as well as among those already on ART and transitioned to DTG-based regimens, the hyperglycemia appears to occur more commonly among the latter group. Adults being initiated on DTG should be screened for risk factors for hyperglycemia: * Age ≥ 40 years * BMI≥ 24 kg/m2 * History of hypertension * Known diabetics should not be initiated or transitioned to DTG. Give an EFV400 or an ATV/r-based regimen. * Clients with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycemia and a high baseline RBS or FBS should not be initiated/transitioned to DTG.
